blocker.summary: The r399-r431 investigation chain is CLOSED -- allocator (r413-r415), shutdown hang (r420-r422/r424), and presentation (r427-r431) are all fixed and live-verified, no known blocker remains. r432 attempted the lowest-cost open thread named by r431 (the dedicated Vulkan/pinned-shader backlog audit r424 had flagged) and found two things. First: a genuine regression in r430's own fix, caught only by a truly clean rebuild (CMake reconfigured from scratch, all 123 targets, not the targeted probe-entry launches that validated r430) -- r430's direct present_to_offscreen() call fired unconditionally, double-presenting in the specific unit-test fallback path (readback_==0, guest_vd_service_present_executes_offscreen expects present_count()==2, got 3). Fixed with a readback_ != 0u guard, the same condition already used nearby to distinguish the real retail path from that test fixture; full ctest 11/11 after the fix, real probe launch unaffected (presented_frames=5 state=2 unchanged). Second, and left as an open decision rather than acted on: git status revealed the native/ backlog is far larger than r424 characterized as 'the Vulkan backlog' -- native_guest_media, native_guest_memory, native_shader_translator, native_xenos, and test files are ALL modified uncommitted too, not just the Vulkan device/pinned-shader files. Deliberately did NOT bulk-commit this wider backlog -- disproportionate for an autonomous continuation cycle to decide alone, and this project has repeatedly treated the standing uncommitted-tree situation as the user's decision across every report since r423. Only the narrow, well-tested regression fix (native_guest_vd.cpp) was committed. Named for r433, only if the user wants to pursue it: catalog the wider native/ backlog precisely (which files, which cycles) before any commit decision, file by file, with the same full-clean-rebuild rigor that caught this cycle's regression -- do not assume the rest is equally safe just because this one file was. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion, now known to be wider than previously described) remains the user's decision, untouched beyond the narrow fixes already disclosed in r413-r432's own reports.
